newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hails courage of Algerian voters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hails courage of Algerian voters.

text.p: The United States saluted the courage of citizens who voted on Thursday in national elections in Algeria, where political violence has claimed 60,000 lives over the past five years.
But the State Department said it was too early to say whether the elections -- the first since violence blamed by Algerian officials on Moslem fundamentalists erupted in 1992 -- were free and fair.

"What is clear to us is that the Algerian people are showing courage by voting in very large numbers, including a very large number of women who are seen to be voting," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"Courage because they have been subjected to the most vicious campaign of terrorism over many, many years."
Official figures issued an hour before most polling stations closed put turnout at just over 56 percent.

Burns said it was "too early to conclude whether or not today's voting would meet an international standard of free and fair elections," although he noted that a number of U.S. and other foreign monitors were observing the vote.
The State Department said on Wednesday it hoped the election would help to put an end to bloodshed in Algeria.
